novelty_basis: OEIS: no match for the row (2, 1, 4, 3, 8, 9, 10, 5, ...), for |g(b) - b| or for g(b) XOR b; text searches for greedy XOR-avoiding permutations found unrelated entries (A109812, A357578); a web search found no mex recursion of this form (closest: Multiplicative Modular Nim, arXiv:2507.08830, a different recursion). Small.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C07.md Theorem 3, induction over Jacobsthal blocks using J_(k+1) + J_k = 2^k and bit estimates); formula verified for all b < 2^15 by an independent bitset implementation (EXP-C07-03); awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
For the mex operation D[x^y], f(a,b) = mex{f(a',b) XOR f(a,b') : a' < a, b' < b}: f(0,b) = 0, f(1,b) = b, and
g(b) = f(2,b) satisfies g(0) = 0 and, for every k >= 1, g(b) = b + J_k for 2^k - J_k <= b < 2^k and
g(b) = b - J_k for 2^k <= b < 2^k + J_k, where J_k = (2^k - (-1)^k)/3 are the Jacobsthal numbers. Equivalently,
g(b) is the least v with v and v XOR b both outside {g(b') : b' < b}. The row is an involution and is not
additively periodic.
title: The Jacobsthal row: row 2 of f(a,b) = mex{f(a',b) XOR f(a,b')} swaps the blocks [2^k - J_k, 2^k) and [2^k, 2^k + J_k)
